mandate.intro: Heritage Foundation's Mandate for Leadership (2023) is the Project 2025 policy book. Each row quotes a Mandate proposal with its page, then the bill or vote it matches. “Direct” means the Mandate names the bill or the same action; “same target” means the bill acts on the same subject in the Mandate's direction; “partial” says exactly where the bill differs. A match shows alignment of policy, not intent or coordination.

items.proposal: Enact the Midnight Rules Relief Act, so several late-term regulations can be disapproved together
items.quote: Congress and the President should enact the Midnight Rules Relief Act
items.match: The Mandate names this bill. H.R. 77 provides for en bloc consideration of resolutions disapproving “midnight rules.”

items.proposal: Prevent a central bank digital currency
items.quote: Prevent the institution of a central bank digital currency (CBDC).
items.match: H.R. 1919 prohibits the use of a central bank digital currency for monetary policy and bars Federal Reserve banks from offering certain products directly to individuals.

items.proposal: Limit California's Clean Air Act waiver
items.quote: Restore the position that California’s waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
items.match: The Mandate calls for narrowing California's waiver. H.J.Res. 87 uses the Congressional Review Act to nullify EPA's waiver decision on Advanced Clean Trucks and related rules.

items.proposal: Limit California's Clean Air Act waiver
items.quote: Restore the position that California’s waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
items.match: H.J.Res. 88 nullifies EPA's waiver decision on California's Advanced Clean Cars II rule.

items.proposal: Limit California's Clean Air Act waiver
items.quote: Restore the position that California’s waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
items.match: H.J.Res. 89 nullifies EPA's waiver decision on California's “Omnibus” low-NOx regulation.

items.quote: Add work requirements and match Medicaid benefits to beneficiary needs.
items.match: Section 71119 requires states to set Medicaid community engagement requirements for certain adults. This is the House vote on passing the bill.
items.bill: H.R. 1, One Big Beautiful Bill Act (as enrolled, Public Law 119-21)

items.quote: Add work requirements and match Medicaid benefits to beneficiary needs.
items.match: The same Section 71119 stayed in the version the House voted to send to the President.

items.proposal: End federal funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting through the budget process
items.quote: Cutting off the CPB is logistically easy. The solution lies in the budgetary process.
items.match: H.R. 4 rescinds the Corporation for Public Broadcasting's fiscal 2026 and 2027 funds.

items.quote: Congress should eliminate ambiguous discretionary language in Title 8 that aliens “may” be detained and clarify that aliens “shall” be detained.
items.match: Same mechanism, narrower scope: S. 5 requires detention of certain aliens charged with or arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, shoplifting or assault of a law enforcement officer.

items.proposal: Enforce and strengthen Section 117 reporting of foreign gifts to universities
items.quote: Reverse the Biden Administration’s refusal to enforce Section 117 of the HEA
items.match: Same provision, different remedy: H.R. 1048 rewrites Section 117 with a $50,000 reporting threshold and fines. The Mandate's further proposal, tying reporting to federal aid, is not in the bill.

method.text: This is not an exhaustive review. The Mandate has no index of bills, so the matches come from searching its text for subjects that bills in this Congress address. 130 measures had a White House statement (the set on the Trump section above). The 11 subjects below were searched; 7 had a Mandate proposal that the measures voted on follow, listed in the table, covering 9 measures and 10 votes. 3 were read and rejected and 1 had no Mandate text. The other measures were not individually checked against the Mandate, so more matches may exist. Two matches are marked partial and say exactly how the bill differs from the Mandate. Mandate matches apply to Republican members only; they are one signal among several, not a symmetrical measure like the Trump votes.
